previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of COPD, chronic DVT/PE, atrial myxoma, and chronic pain was admitted for bilateral lower extremity swelling and dyspnea. He had worsening right leg swelling two days prior, followed by left leg involvement, and reported shortness of breath with ambulation and cough. Initial workup ruled out pulmonary embolism and infection. Elevated BNP and clinical findings suggested new-onset heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Edema improved with IV diuresis, and dyspnea resolved with bronchodilators and optimized COPD management. High sodium intake from V8 juice and recent high-dose prednisone were identified as contributing factors. The patient remained hemodynamically stable, with improved symptoms and near-resolution of edema at discharge. Social work addressed homelessness, though the patient declined shelter referrals. A follow-up appointment was arranged, and he was discharged home with a plan to continue anticoagulation, diuresis, and respiratory medications.

Patient initially presented with reported subacute progression

hospitalizations elsewhere without improvement in his symptoms.  
He was not hypoxic at rest or with ambulation, and given lack of 
improvement with prolonged steroid treatment at OSH, his 
presentation did not seem consistent with a COPD exacerbation.  
CTA chest  was negative for PNA or PE--it did show incidental 
stenosis of his L PA artery which did not require any urgent

serial cardiac biomarkers showed no evidence of acute ischemia.

mismatch, but per pulmonary evaluation, was not felt to 
represent acute pulmonary embolism and was of uncertain 
significance.  Coronary evaluation with pharmacologic stress 
test was reassuring.   Additional workup from ___, 
and ___ was obtained without any remarkable findings. 
Was kept overnight for ?hemoptysis on night prior to discharge, 
though per RN report it was possible that blood came from 
midline and was not actually expectorated. Pulm thought that it 
could be due to excessive coughing with anticoagulation. After 
overnight monitoring, no further hemoptysis so felt safe for 
discharge. Concerns regarding behavioral issues and secondary 
gain as below

# Concern for secondary gain / behavioral issues - Admission 
notable for warning signs for behavioral component to symptoms 
and concern for secondary gains. He was never hypoxic and always 
able to augment his oxygen sats while walking, with breathing 
noted to be clear and comfortable until one asks to auscultate

in his car, drives around the state from hospital to hospital,

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CTA CHEST WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION:  History: ___ with CP, SOB, hx multiple PEs.// PE?

TECHNIQUE:  Axial multidetector CT images were obtained through the thorax
after the uneventful administration of intravenous contrast.  Reformatted
coronal, sagittal, thin slice axial images, and oblique maximal intensity
projection images were submitted to PACS and reviewed.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 734 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CTA chest from ___

FINDINGS: 

HEART AND VASCULATURE: Of note, this exam is moderately limited by respiratory
motion artifact.  Within these limitations, the pulmonary vasculature is well
opacified to the segmental level without filling defect to indicate a
pulmonary embolus. There is focal narrowing and weblike scar with poststenotic
dilatation in the left lower lobe segmental artery, which is proximal to the
superior segmental artery.  There appear to be changes from chronic pulmonary
emboli in the subsegmental arteries in the right lower lobe, however, this
study is suboptimal for definitive assessment.  The thoracic aorta is normal
in caliber without evidence of dissection or intramural hematoma.  The heart,
pericardium, and great vessels are within normal limits. No pericardial
effusion is seen.
AXILLA, HILA, AND MEDIASTINUM: No axillary, mediastinal, or hilar
lymphadenopathy is present.  No mediastinal mass.


PLEURAL SPACES: No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

LUNGS/AIRWAYS: There is mild dependent atelectasis.  No focal consolidations
identified.  The airways are patent to the level of the segmental bronchi
bilaterally.

BASE OF NECK: Visualized portions of the base of the neck show no abnormality.

ABDOMEN:  Included portion of the upper abdomen is remarkable for hepatic
steatosis with enlargement of the left hepatic lobe.  There is a band or scar
in the right hepatic lobe, which courses to the dome of the diaphragm.

BONES: No suspicious osseous abnormality is seen.? There is no acute fracture.


IMPRESSION: 

1.  The exam is moderately limited by respiratory motion artifact.  Within
these limitations, the pulmonary vasculature is well opacified to the
segmental level without filling defect to indicate a pulmonary embolus.  No
evidence of aortic abnormality.
